explanation: Singapore has no real tipping culture; many sit-down restaurants already add a 10% service charge (shown as "++" on menus) plus GST, so an extra tip is not expected. Leaving a small amount for great service is not rude, just unnecessary, and it is never expected at hawker centres, cafes, or bars.
local_tip: Check your bill for the "++" service charge before adding anything extra; if you do want to tip for excellent service, hand it directly to the staff member rather than leaving it on the table.
regional_note: Hawker centres, food courts, and casual cafes rarely add a service charge and tipping there is unusual; upscale restaurants and hotels catering to tourists or expats see occasional voluntary tipping.

also_check.note: Tipping is considered confusing or insulting since good service is already the standard; servers may try to return the money.
Tipping 15-20% at sit-down restaurants is standard and service staff rely on it as part of their income.
A service charge is included by law, so extra tipping is optional but rounding up or leaving small change is appreciated.
